gate1.note: User selected Feature + Autopilot at the front door after being shown the measured root cause. A production BFF session survives exactly one refresh: the Hub rotates its session cookie as __Host-fxl_hub_session in production, and hub-sdk 1.3.1's parseRotatedRefresh regex cannot match a name preceded by '-', so tx.update is never called and the store replays a stale refresh token until the Hub revokes the family with reuse_detected. Invisible locally because the Hub only prefixes the cookie when NODE_ENV=production, which is why three prior browser-side fixes all missed it. Four independent slices in one wave: slice 01 normalizes the rotated cookie name at createHubBff's fetchImpl seam and adds the end-to-end oracle that was missing; slices 02-04 repair the /no-role dead end that earlier fixes turned a lost session into. Gate 2 remains mandatory per slice and per wave. Gate 3 remains human-gated; this run stops at master.
gate1.outcome: All four slices merged to master and each passed Gate 2 by a separate Verify agent, plus a wave-verify on integrated master (1203 tests, lint, type-check, real build, security review). Root cause was upstream of this repo: hub-sdk 1.3.1's parseRotatedRefresh cannot match the __Host-fxl_hub_session name the Hub uses in production. Fixed here at createHubBff's fetchImpl seam; the real one-line SDK fix is filed in nexo/ROADMAP.md for 16--INTERNAL--fxl-hub. Wave ran serially because nexo-wave-exec.sh hardcodes the 'main' trunk and pnpm worktrees lack node_modules; Gate 2 was not weakened. Mutation tooling is not configured, so per-slice mutation proofs stood in. Not promoted: this run stops at master pending the operator's own check.

MAJOR bump, and the labels did not understate it: two refactor(auth)! commits carry BREAKING CHANGE footers for the three variables that moved off the FXL_HUB_ namespace. The break is entirely ENVIRONMENTAL - no code contract changed shape the way v3.0.0's access gate did - and SALES_SESSION_ENCRYPTION_IKM is what makes it major: it is the HKDF input for the session sealer, and an operator who does not carry its value across gets every user logged out once with nothing thrown and nothing logged. Release-verify PASS by a SEPARATE Verify agent on the exact release commit a1be9d6: lint 0, type-check 0, CI=true pnpm test 0 (1309 tests across 103 files - 80 shared-utils, 445 api, 784 web - plus 11 guard tests), a COLD pnpm run build 0 with both tsbuildinfo and all four dist/ deleted first, and 169 integration tests across 25 files, all exit 0. The integration pinning was PROVEN rather than assumed, and the verifier refused the easy argument: fxl-db-server IS resolvable from this machine over Tailscale, so 'staging is unreachable' was not available. The decisive evidence is a measured 2552-transaction delta on pg_stat_database inside the local container across a second full run, plus setup-env.ts's hard assignment resolving to localhost:5006 and the non-superuser fxl_sales_test role being the connecting role. Security review of v3.0.0..a1be9d6 clean on all five axes: no credential value anywhere (both env examples ship every secret slot blank), no changed line touching the single access gate (the four grep hits are comment text; allowWithoutAccess still defaults false and no route mounts requiredModule), zero changed lines touching org scoping or RLS, not one line of apps/web/src changed at all, and no new outbound call - the only dependency movement being the exact-pinned hub-sdk 2.2.0 -> 2.3.0 with a byte-identical transitive tree, which is why the pnpm-workspace.yaml Hono override did not move. ZERO migrations in the range, so rollback is a pure code revert - the same property that made v2.7.2, v2.8.0 and v3.0.0 safe to promote straight through. The topology reinforces it: Vercel builds apps/web from the production branch ONLY, so a staging validation pause would have produced no web deployment to test and bought no signal. Tag v4.0.0 pushed to a1be9d6, master fast-forwarded 6cd9fa4..a1be9d6, staging fast-forwarded 7ddf525..a1be9d6 and production fast-forwarded 7ddf525..a1be9d6; master, staging and production are all at a1be9d6. Every push was a plain non-force push, so git itself enforced fast-forward. FOUR OPERATOR ITEMS WERE OPEN AT THE GATE AND WERE NOT CLOSED BY THIS CUT, approved open on the operator's explicit statement that there are no production users yet, and carried into the next milestone until each is confirmed: FXL_HUB_TRUSTED_ORIGINS must be set in staging and production or every cross-origin POST is 403 origin_not_trusted, reproducing the 2026-08-10 outage, and it was confirmed in the shipped bundle to have NO fallback; FXL_HUB_REDIRECT_URI must be explicit outside development, not because it is required but because its default lands on the Hub's own origin and the boot refuses that origin; the three renamed variables must carry their VALUES, created alongside the old names so a revert inside the rollback window still finds them; and the VITE_* variables on Vercel validate at RENDER rather than at build, so a green build is not evidence the browser can boot.
